Kgothatso Montjane : Wheelchair Wimbledon Champion

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Commission

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Overview:
This feature story will delve into the inspiring journey of three time Grand Slam Champion ,Kgothatso Montjane , a Limpopo-born wheelchair tennis player who has risen to the top ranks of the sport despite numerous challenges. Currently ranked number eight in the world in the women’s division, Montjane’s story is one of resilience, determination, and triumph.

Story Angle:
The narrative will highlight Montjane's early life struggles, her remarkable achievements in both dance and tennis, her contributions to her community, and her recent victory at Wimbledon. It will also touch upon her aspirations and the message she wishes to convey to the world about overcoming disabilities.

Structure:

1. Introduction:
The story will open with a powerful scene-setting introduction that captures the essence of Montjane's origins in Limpopo and her current status as a world-class athlete.

2. Early Life and Challenges:
This section will provide a background on Montjane’s congenital deformity, the amputation of her foot at age 12, and her initial foray into competitive ballroom and Latin-American dance.

3. Discovering Tennis:
The narrative will explore how Montjane was introduced to wheelchair tennis at Helen Franz Special School and how her teachers recognized her talent, leading to her representing the school in Johannesburg.

4. Rising Through the Ranks:
The story will chronicle Montjane’s rise in the international wheelchair tennis circuit, including her participation in major tournaments like the Australian Open, Japan Open, NEC Singles Masters, and the Paralympics.

5. Unbeaten at Home and Giving Back:
This section will focus on Montjane’s unbeaten streak on domestic courts for nine years and her philanthropic efforts through the Kgothatso Montjane Foundation, which provides sports facilities and equipment to disadvantaged communities.

6. Recent Victory and Future Aspirations:
The feature will cover Montjane’s recent Wimbledon women’s doubles victory with Yui Kamiji, her preparation for the upcoming Paralympics, and her broader aspirations, including community projects and business ventures.

7. Conclusion:
The story will conclude with Montjane’s reflections on her journey, the importance of hard work and dedication, and her message to people living with disabilities.

Visuals and Interviews:

Archival footage and photographs of Montjane’s early life, dance competitions, and tennis matches.
Interviews with Montjane, her coaches, family members, and teachers from Helen Franz Special School.
Coverage of her recent Wimbledon victory and homecoming celebration.

Script:


Kgothatso Monjane

Dramatic breather
V/O Each year, the world’s top tennis players gather at Wimbledon, the oldest and most prestigious tournament…held on the iconic grass courts in London, England ,It’s synonymous with excellence and tradition.
V/O But , the Wimbledon title had eluded South African players since the '80s [pause]— until this year, when one of our own finally broke through.
[ transition/fade to black]
Link: Seshego, just outside of Polokwane, a township like many others in South Africa, faces high levels of unemployment and poverty, with few sporting heroes and even fewer sporting facilities. but, against all odds, a Wimbledon Champion has emerged from this very place.
breather- visuals of township Seshego/Polokwane transition to Wimbledon commentary of match]
V/O Local wheelchair tennis star Kgothatso Montjane made history when she won this year’s women’s wheelchair doubles title with Japan’s Yui Kamiji : Marking her place in the history books.
V/O The first time in forty years that a South African has won a Wimbledon final
V/O With 29 singles titles and doubles victories at the French Open and US Open, Kgothatso is one of South Africa's most decorated tennis players. It is this latest win, though, that has truly captured the nation's heart.
Upsound Mac :45:48 Okay. So what is it like being on that hallowed turf?
Upsound Kgothatso45:48, you just feel like a star. I think that when you realize that I'm a star, I'm among the stars because whenever you put your All-White, they call your name.
Upsound Kgothatso : 46:18 . I'm being escorted to the tennis court. [Mac]Guys, it's not that deep. It's just a tennis court. Just a tennis court.
Upsound Kgothatso45:10 South Africa can also be like, we are out there with the world. You know, so that's what fills my heart, that the people are happy
[ breather]
V/O Like her achievements on the court, Kgothatso’s life has been defined by overcoming significant obstacles. Born with a congenital disorder that affected her hands and legs, she had her left leg amputated when she was just 12.
Upsound Kgothatso : 03:00 I went to a special school and I've seen a lot of kids go to hospital, would go and be operated. For me, when it was my turn, I just saw it as one of those.
V/O But in her community, she found it challenging to adjust to life after the amputation.
Upsound Kgothatso : 3:30 [ Mac]Were you treated differently by the other kids?
Upsound Kgothatso :Back home, yes, in the streets, you know. I feel like I was too slow for them, but I didn't know that.03:40 because they didn't want to play with me with other games. But where we're just sitting, it's fine. But where we have to run around, no one wants to play. But it used to not make sense.
V/O Her mother, Margret Montjane, nurtured a sense of independence and pride in her. Bit by bit, Kgothatso found her confidence.
Upsound Margret Montjane [ day 2 interview} 02:27 IKgothatso was always active,that is why I did not notice that she was disabled , she was busy doing chores doing everything like a normal person 03:36//03:44 Kgothatso would go to the streets and play with other children03:50//4:00 and she would stand up for herself4:03
Upsound Mac 07:04 When would you say the bug bit for tennis?

Upsound Kgothatso 0:48I personally wasn't so keen to do it. But the school or the teacher wasn't asking me if can you go and try it. They were telling me you're going to go and try it and represent the school.

V/O With no tennis facilities, the budding player had to be resourceful.

Upsound Kgothatso : 01:18 We used to play in the school hall and divide the entire hall with chairs. And yeah, the other one will be on the other side. , we didn't have like the right time.01:48 dimensions of the court, we didn't even mark up the lines.

V/O But Kgothathso’s natural talent soon saw her excelling at provincial level, and then earning her national colors.

Upsound Margret Montjane 09:48[ Day 2 interview] there were so many cups, we didnt know where to put them,we were happy supporting her 09:59

[breather/transition Australian open general visuals ]


V/O In 2013, destiny knocked on the door when rookie Kgothatso earned her place in one of the four major international tennis tournaments: the Australian Open.

Upsound Kgothatso 07:43 This is a good opportunity to travel, see the world.. I was still young. I was like,, so there are Grand Slams and the other tournaments. I'm like...

Upsound Kgothatso 7:27 I'm there, everyone is talking about wanting to watch Serena, Roger Federer. I mean, I'm just like, who are those people?

V/O Although she didn’t reach the final stages, she was steadily carving out a name for herself in the world of wheelchair tennis…
[change of music to pensive/tense]

V/O But just 5 years later, her promising career was under threat.

Upsound Kgothatso : 10:23 Definitely. 2018, yeah, just the end of my career, actually, because we didn't have any sponsors.10:52 wheelchair tennis wasn't funded anymore. And as athletes or as players, we needed to go out and look for our own sponsorships

V/O Tennis is an expensive sport, and losing sponsorships meant Kgothatso couldn't afford to compete at the highest level.

Upsound Kgothatso 10:52 I told myself,11:09
drafting a sponsorship proposal, learning from Google samples, and yeah, trying to send to people who I thought would really help.

Upsound Kgothatso 13:01 I started studying to try to revamp my CV. Even though I was worried, I have no work experience.

V/O Fortunately, Kgothathso did not have to give up her dream. Her search for new sponsors paid off, and with the support of a sports management company and former First Lady Zanele Mbeki, she was back on track.

V/ 0 Though she continues to compete, she’s now committed to paving the way for younger players. manager, Thabo Sephuma, she has started a foundation to build facilities for disabled students.

Upsound Thabo 05:50 [ Day two] that's one part that is very exciting. We really want to plough back to the community through infrastructure building, in particular in the community that needs help. 06:26 kids with disabilities they are looked the other way around, they're not given a chance.


Upsound Kgothatso 31:14 I don't want the next generation to suffer like I did

V/O Feeling inspired—or perhaps a bit overzealous—I couldn’t resist challenging the champ.
[ tennis sequence ]


V/O The women’s doubles final on Wimbledon’s iconic Centre Court this month was the most important match of Kgothathso’s life: the culmination of countless struggles and near misses.

Upsound Mac 40:52 that moment, take us through it. What was going through the mind?
[build tension]

Kgothatso Montjane 40:52I was the one serving for the championship, rI lost my first serve and we were two love down.

Kgothatso Montjane 41:44 I like visualized, breathed.This is the moment where you're going to make it. [build tension]


V/O Years of experience played their part, and she held her nerve.

Upsound Kgothatso 43:10They played back to me. I played shorter. I'm just going to play tactics. I played over her head, and her partner gets the ball, plays it back to me. I'm like, even better. Game-safe match. I'm going to play a drop shot. And I see her

Upsound Kgothatso 43:38 pushing and pushing and pushing and reaching. And I just hear Yui at the back saying, come on and I was just telling them like, we did it [.Mac ] Wow.
[ breath/ maybe use an upsound as she is driving in]


V/O: This week, Polokwane erupted in celebration as Kgothatso brought her trophy home.

V/O… An icon of the game, Kgothatso has not only shown us what’s possible but has inspired a generation to reach for their dreams.

[ end]

UPSOUND: Speech after winning Wimbledon

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Overview: This feature story will delve into the inspiring journey of three time Grand Slam Champion ,Kgothatso Montjane , a Limpopo-born wheelchair tennis player who has risen to the top ranks of the sport despite numerous challenges. Currently ranked number eight in the world in the women’s division, Montjane’s story is one of resilience, determination, and triumph. Story Angle: The narrative will highlight Montjane's early life struggles, her remarkable achievements in both dance and tennis, her contributions to her community, and her recent victory at Wimbledon. It will also touch upon her aspirations and the message she wishes to convey to the world about overcoming disabilities. Structure: 1. Introduction: The story will open with a powerful scene-setting introduction that captures the essence of Montjane's origins in Limpopo and her current status as a world-class athlete. 2. Early Life and Challenges: This section will provide a background on Montjane’s congenital deformity, the amputation of her foot at age 12, and her initial foray into competitive ballroom and Latin-American dance. 3. Discovering Tennis: The narrative will explore how Montjane was introduced to wheelchair tennis at Helen Franz Special School and how her teachers recognized her talent, leading to her representing the school in Johannesburg. 4. Rising Through the Ranks: The story will chronicle Montjane’s rise in the international wheelchair tennis circuit, including her participation in major tournaments like the Australian Open, Japan Open, NEC Singles Masters, and the Paralympics. 5. Unbeaten at Home and Giving Back: This section will focus on Montjane’s unbeaten streak on domestic courts for nine years and her philanthropic efforts through the Kgothatso Montjane Foundation, which provides sports facilities and equipment to disadvantaged communities. 6. Recent Victory and Future Aspirations: The feature will cover Montjane’s recent Wimbledon women’s doubles victory with Yui Kamiji, her preparation for the upcoming Paralympics, and her broader aspirations, including community projects and business ventures. 7. Conclusion: The story will conclude with Montjane’s reflections on her journey, the importance of hard work and dedication, and her message to people living with disabilities. Visuals and Interviews: Archival footage and photographs of Montjane’s early life, dance competitions, and tennis matches. Interviews with Montjane, her coaches, family members, and teachers from Helen Franz Special School. Coverage of her recent Wimbledon victory and homecoming celebration.
